channel.title: Objective Daily News
channel.description: An archival service and a captain's log of the news: the desk's analysis, stamped objective, and the world's reporting filed beneath it, stamped subjective. Founded 2026.

item.title: Inflation Prints Hot at 3.3 Percent and Growth Is Revised to 4.3 Percent as Wall Street Falls Again, Washington Proposes Tariffs on Fourteen Partners, and Ukraine Counts Seven Dead While Kyiv Hits Three Refineries
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midday file for Wednesday, November 25, 2026: the October core PCE price index rises 3.3 percent from a year earlier, above the 3.2 percent expected, and headline PCE rises 3.8 percent, in the Bureau of Economic Analysis figures; third-quarter product is revised sharply higher to a 4.3 percent annual rate from the advance estimate of 3.4 percent; durable goods orders rise 0.2 percent and jobless claims fall to 189,000; new-home sales jump 14.2 percent to 701,000 after September is revised down to 614,000; Wall Street falls again in the morning, the Dow down more than 800 points and the Nasdaq down 3.9 percent in the live account, with Dell down 10 percent after its record quarter; the Trade Representative makes determinations against 14 economies in the excess-capacity investigations and proposes tariffs, with China at 20 percent on top of its first-term duties and Mexico and Norway left undetermined; the fuller wire account of the Ras Tanura claim carries satellite imagery of black smoke over about 600 square kilometres, with no word from Aramco or the government communications office; Tehran warns ships to coordinate passage of the strait as the visible counter counts three crossings on Wednesday; Ukraine counts at least seven dead in six regions from the night’s 112 drones, and Kyiv’s drones hit three Russian refineries and an airbase; and Russia’s defence ministry files no word on the Merkury into a fifth day. Collected at 1200.

item.title: Dictator and Authoritarian: The Definitions, the President's Own Words, and the Record of the Labels in American Politics
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: What the reference books say the words dictator and authoritarian mean; President Donald Trump's own statements about the label in 2023, 2025, and 2026; his critics' statements; the American Presidency Project's executive-order count; and the documented record of political labels adopted by their targets, from Yankee Doodle to the Vermin Club to the basket of deplorables.

item.title: Asia Gives Back the Huang Rally in a Morning, the Houthis Claim the Riyadh Tower and a Refinery at Ras Tanura, Tehran Counts Two More Tankers on Mines Against Four Crossings in the Visible Counter, and Moscow Files No Word on the Merkury Into a Fifth Day
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The overnight file for Wednesday, November 25, 2026: Asia reverses the rally that followed Jensen Huang’s return, with the broad Asia-Pacific index down 2.3 percent in one wire reading and 3.2 percent in another, South Korea down as much as 5.3 percent in one and 6.4 percent in another, and Taiwan down 5.1 percent at its worst in one and 8.6 percent in another, as reports say the United States Trade Representative is preparing findings on excess industrial capacity among 16 trading partners that could open the way to new tariffs; Dell Technologies rises 4.1 percent in after-hours trade in the wire account, settling the direction the Midnight Watch left disputed, on the record quarter the company filed after Tuesday’s bell; the Houthis claim Wednesday attacks on the Ras Tanura refinery and on Riyadh’s financial district in three phases, and the coalition says its defences destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura, a day after the second strike on the Public Investment Fund tower wounded 11; Ukraine’s air force counts 112 drones in the night, 88 brought down, with hits at 18 locations, on top of Tuesday night’s two dead in the Odesa region and two injured in Kyiv; Tehran counts two more tankers on mines on Wednesday, against a visible counter that corrects Tuesday to four crossings and counts none yet on Wednesday; the hearing dates for the ground stop are set, December 1 in the House and December 2 in the Senate, with the findings still unreleased; and Russia’s defence ministry files no word on the Merkury into a fifth day. Collected at 0400.

item.title: Tuesday Closes With the Futures Down and Nvidia Down Again in Late Trade, Dell's Record Quarter Beaten in the Session and Disputed After It, Anthropic Under Its Offering Price, a Second Strike on Riyadh's Tallest Tower, and New Dead in Odesa and Kyiv While Moscow Files No Word on the Merkury Into a Fourth Day
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midnight file for Wednesday, November 25, 2026: what Tuesday settled and what it left open. The futures fall after Tuesday’s split close, Dow futures down 0.3 percent and Nasdaq-100 futures down 0.8 percent in one late reading and down 1.17 percent in another, with Nvidia down 2 percent in late trade after its 5.9 percent session fall; Dell Technologies reports a record fiscal third quarter after the bell, revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103 percent, and adjusted earnings of $9.45 a share against estimates near $6.60, after falling nearly 12 percent in the session, and the after-hours accounts disagree on whether it rose or fell overnight; Anthropic closes at $81.91, down 6.5 percent, below its $83 offering price for the first time; President Trump tells the New York Post it is probably not too late for the United States to take an equity stake in Nvidia; investigators into the November 13 ground stop have recreated the failure in a laboratory and point to an overlooked router setting, with a report in preparation and the formal findings still unreleased; late strikes kill two in the Odesa region and injure two in Kyiv; a drone strikes Riyadh’s Public Investment Fund tower a second time in a week, wounding 11; Tehran’s tanker counts reach four for Tuesday and six in two days with no vessel named, while the visible counter closes Tuesday at three crossings; and Russia’s defence ministry files no word on the Merkury into a fourth day. Collected at 0000.

item.title: The Dow Closes Above 50,000 as the Nasdaq Falls on Nvidia's Retreat, Dymer's Toll Rises to Twelve, and Mr. Sullivan Concedes in Alaska While Poland Renews Its Push for American Troops
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The evening file for Tuesday, November 24, 2026: the Dow closes at 50,026.46, up 0.87 percent, while the S&P 500 falls 0.48 percent to 7,202.45 and the Nasdaq falls about 1.5 percent as Nvidia gives back 5.86 percent to $155.38 after Monday’s 31 percent rise; consumer confidence stands at 103.3, the highest since January 2025, on a survey that closed November 17; Dymer’s toll rises to 12 when the woman of 79 pulled alive from the rubble dies in hospital; Alaska’s certified result stands at 144,583 votes for Ms. Peltola, 50.14 percent, to 132,022 for Mr. Sullivan, who concedes on Tuesday; Poland renews its push for a permanent American presence after Monday night’s drone; Iran’s counts of tankers on mines stand at two, three and four in its own services’ statements, with no vessel named and no confirmation from an outside authority in the file; and Brent settles at $91.40, up 2.27 percent, after touching a three-month low in the morning. Collected at 1800.

item.title: Wall Street Splits at Midday as the Dow Rises and the Nasdaq Gives Back Monday's Rally, Confidence Surges to 103.3, and Poland Calls Monday Night's Drone Intentional While Tehran Orders the Strait Closed Further
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midday file for Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Wall Street splits in the morning after Monday’s rally, with the Dow up 0.41 percent to 49,797.36 at 0954 Eastern, the S&P 500 down 0.47 percent to 7,203.27 and the Nasdaq down 1.21 percent to 23,798.24, and Nvidia down 5.8 percent, in the wire account; Asia’s leap stands as the overnight file printed it, at 7.5 percent in Seoul, 9.1 percent in Taiwan and 4.5 percent in Tokyo in the wire’s figures; consumer confidence jumps 11.4 points to 103.3, its highest since January 2025, on a survey that closed November 17; Poland says Monday night’s drone incursion was intentional, with a shootdown authorised and held; Iran’s army chief orders the Strait of Hormuz closed further day by day until seven conditions are met; the Treasury’s $14.7 billion shadow-banking figure stands in the department’s own release; and the router installs the senators asked paused were already paused on November 18. Collected at 1200.

item.title: The Lucia Prologue in Grand Theft Auto VI: Payday Loans, Eviction Notices, Deactivated Accounts, and the Call That Follows
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The documented record behind the opening sequence of Grand Theft Auto VI, released November 19, 2026: the payday-loan market as the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau measured it, driver deactivation as surveyed in New York in 2025, eviction filings as tracked by Princeton's Eviction Lab, child-welfare intake as reported by the Children's Bureau for fiscal 2023, kinship placement in the federal foster-care data, and the call volumes and measured burnout of the workers who receive such afternoons as routine, printed whole.

item.title: The Fasces: The Bundle of Sticks in Rome, in the Fable, in American Symbols, in the Five Arrows, and in the English Word
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The documented record of the fasces, the bound bundle of rods carried before Roman magistrates: its Etruscan remains and Roman use, the Aesop fable of the bundle of sticks and its travels to Scythia and Mongolia, the bundle's place in the civic symbols of the United States, France, and Ecuador, the Haudenosaunee teaching of the five arrows and its documented place in American confederal history, the Italian word fascio and the movement that took the name in 1919, the definitions of fascism recorded by its own Doctrine and by the scholars Paxton, Eco, and Griffin, the bundle on the banners of the labor unions, the English word faggot in its bundle sense, and the Anti-Defamation League's entry on the symbol, printed whole.

item.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated: The Unanimous Vote, the Government’s Input, and the Investigation That Continues
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The documented record of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s president, chief executive, and director on November 23, 2026: the board’s unanimous vote eleven days after it accepted his resignation and six days after it said he would not return, the government input the board cited, the White House effort reported behind it, the market’s 31 percent answer, and the investigation and probes that did not end, printed whole.

item.title: COP31: The Split Presidency, the Missing Words, and the Pact That Failed
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The documented record of COP31 at Antalya: the split Turkish-Australian presidency struck at Belém, the cover decision whose fossil-fuel language was present in the first draft and absent from the last, the closing plenary that rejected the Antalya Pact on November 22, 2026, the Article 6, just-transition, adaptation and finance decisions adopted anyway, and what travels to Bonn and COP32 at Addis Ababa, printed whole.

item.title: Asia Leaps on Mr. Huang's Return With Seoul Up Seven Percent and Taipei Nine, the Guards Count Three Tankers on Mines Against Four Announced at Midnight, and NATO Sends an AWACS to Poland While Moscow Files No Word on the Merkury for a Third Day
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The overnight file for Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Asia leaps on Jensen Huang’s return, with South Korea’s Kospi up about 7.5 percent, Taiwan up 9.1 percent and Japan’s Nikkei up 4.5 percent in the wire account, while United States futures stand flat; the Guards’ navy says three violating oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, in the wire form of Tehran’s announcement, against four tankers announced in the roundup the Midnight Watch filed, with none named in either form and no answer from Central Command; NATO authorises the forward deployment of an AWACS aircraft to Poland after the North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels on the three Kh-101 missiles; Russia’s defence ministry files no word on the Merkury for a third day; Dymer’s search stands ended at a final eleven, with two names still being established; the Treasury sanctions more than two dozen exchange houses, front companies and people in Iran’s shadow banking networks and reports about $14.7 billion in transactions; and the ground stop’s findings stand unreleased, with senators asking for a pause on the router installs. Collected at 0400.

item.title: Monday Closes With Dymer's Search Ended at a Final Eleven, HPE Beating the Street After the Bell and Falling After Hours, and Four Tankers Claimed on Mines in the Strait With None Named
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midnight file for Tuesday, November 24, 2026: what Monday settled and what it left open. The search in Dymer ends on Monday evening with a final toll of 11 dead and five injured in hospital, the Interior Ministry reports, closing the count the day carried open at two unknown; Hewlett Packard Enterprise reports after the bell with revenue of $14.55 billion, up 50 percent, and adjusted earnings of $1.43 a share against estimates near $1.28, raises its fiscal 2027 outlook, and falls in after-hours trading by 5.7 percent in one reading and 8 percent in another; the futures stand slightly higher at the turn of the log after Wall Street’s best day since April 9, 2025; Iran announces that four oil tankers struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, two of them traveling with Central Command support, names none of them, and its courts’ $290 billion compensation ruling against the United States is reported the same day, while the strait’s visible counter closes Monday at four crossings; Russia’s defence ministry files no word on the Merkury for a second day; and the ground stop’s root-cause findings stand unreleased past the administrator’s own Friday and the Senate’s Monday. Collected at 0000.

item.title: Aphantasia: The Naming, the Numbers, and the Effort to Measure an Absence
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The documented record of aphantasia: Galton’s 1880 description and the century that set it aside, the 2015 naming by Adam Zeman, the public discoveries of Blake Ross, Ed Catmull and Glen Keane, the competing prevalence figures and the questionnaire cutoffs that produce them, the priming, pupil and 7-Tesla measurements, and the record on memory, faces and the other senses, printed whole.

item.title: Wall Street Posts Its Best Day Since April 2025 as Nvidia Gains 31 Percent on Mr. Huang's Return, NATO Sends an AWACS to Poland, and Dymer's Search Goes On With Two Still Unknown
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The evening file for Monday, November 23, 2026: Wall Street closes with its best day since April 9, 2025, the S&P 500 up 4.73 percent to 7,237.17, the Nasdaq Composite up 6.51 percent to 24,089.56 and the Dow up 1,447.98 points, as Nvidia gains 31.48 percent to $165.05 on its board’s unanimous reinstatement of Jensen Huang, its best day since 2003, adding roughly $950 billion in value, while Anthropic falls 1.43 percent to $87.64 against the rally; President Trump takes credit on CNBC, saying he convinced the board, and Democratic leaders and two Republican members of Congress answer in the other direction; the North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels and the alliance authorizes a forward AWACS deployment to Poland, holding Russia fully responsible for the three Kh-101 missiles; Moscow’s defence ministry still files no word on the Merkury at Benghazi while Russia’s ambassador in Libya calls the attacks terrorist and says they will not go unanswered; Dymer’s toll stands at 11 with two people still unknown on the region’s day of mourning; more than 60 aviation groups ask Congress for at least $30 billion while the ground stop’s root cause, promised by Friday, still stands unreleased on the day the Senate’s answers fall due; and the strait counts four crossings for Monday in the visible counter. Collected at 1800.

item.title: Nvidia's Board Brings Back Mr. Huang and Wall Street Leaps With Him, Moscow Answers Benghazi With 'Taken Note,' and Dymer's Missing Fall to Two
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midday file for Monday, November 23, 2026: Nvidia’s board votes unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board director, effective immediately, saying it received input from senior levels of the United States government and is confident his return poses no national security risk, and the market answers with Nvidia up about a third, the Nasdaq up about 6 percent, the S&P 500 up about 4 percent and the Dow up about 1,300 points at midday, while Anthropic stands little changed near $89; Moscow answers the Benghazi claim in the Kremlin spokesman’s words—Russia has ‘taken note’ and the defence ministry is handling it—against Kyiv’s ‘exemplary operation’; Dymer’s toll stands at 11 with the fate of two people still unknown, against the eleven sought on Sunday, and the wider Kyiv region count reaches at least 15; the flash purchasing managers’ readings ease to 54.6 composite in the United States while Germany jumps to 55.0; and the strait counts one crossing by midday and corrects Sunday to three. Collected at 1200.

item.title: The Politics of The Hunger Games: The Author’s Record, the Text, and the Fight Over Its Name
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The documented record of the politics of The Hunger Games: what Suzanne Collins said she built, what the text contains, the Treaty of Treason with the Versailles record printed beside it, the Capitol’s stated protection bargain, the scholarship, the appropriation record, and the labeling fight of November 2026, printed whole as the sixth film opens.

item.title: Kyiv Claims the Benghazi Sinking in Its Own Word, Dymer's Toll Reaches Eleven With a Woman of Seventy-Nine Pulled Alive, and Asia Holds the Futures Bounce While Seoul Falls Again
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The overnight file for Monday, November 23, 2026: President Zelensky says on Monday that Ukraine sank the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi with seven naval drones, destroyed a Ka-27 helicopter with her, and hit a second ship he names as the dry cargo vessel MV Angara, while Russia has not yet commented in the file and the second ship stands under three names in three accounts; Dymer’s toll reaches 11 in the regional governor’s Monday word, with a 79-year-old woman pulled alive after 22 hours in the rubble beside the boy rescued on Sunday; the North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels today on the three objects Poland now confirms were Kh-101 missiles; the strait counts its first Monday crossing, the tanker Musik inbound, after closing Sunday at two; Asia holds the futures bounce while Seoul falls again and China cuts its margin requirement; and Spain enters its five-day poll ban with its final poll nine-tenths of a point apart. Collected at 0400.

item.title: Sunday Closes With a Boy Pulled Alive From Dymer's Rubble, a Russian Corvette Sunk at Her Berth in Benghazi, and the Futures Up Two Percent at the Turn of the Log
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midnight file for Monday, November 23, 2026: what Sunday settled and what it left open. A seven-year-old boy is pulled alive from the rubble of the Dymer apartment building after nearly 14 hours, while the town’s toll is counted at four by the President and at nine in the regional head’s later word, with 11 people still sought; the Russian corvette Merkury capsizes and sinks at Benghazi after two sea drones strike her at her berth, a second commercial ship is hit off the port in the evening, and Kyiv claims nothing; COP31’s collapse is laid to one delegation’s access in the first full post-mortem; Bahrain’s claimed radars end the day with no American answer; the strait closes Sunday at two crossings; and the futures reopen up two percent with Bitcoin’s Sunday close at $60,784. Collected at 0000.

item.title: The Sparta II Goes Out Under Tow With Her Containers Still Warm, Dymer Counts Four Dead With Ten Still in the Rubble, and COP31 Ends in Antalya With No Deal and the Words Fossil Fuels Unwritten
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The evening file for Sunday, November 22, 2026: the Sparta II is towed out of Finnish waters by the Russian rescue vessel Murman after seven vessels of three countries fought her fire, her containers still warm and one of her 16 crew slightly injured; a Russian drone strike on a five-storey building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, leaves four dead in the region, about ten people still trapped and 14 out of contact, with the rescue halted in the afternoon by a new aerial threat; Bahrain’s two injured stand as the Arab League, the Gulf Cooperation Council and the Arab Parliament condemn the attack and Manama holds that the site hit was purely civilian, while no American statement on the claimed Patriot radars stands in the file; the strait’s visible counter closes Sunday at two crossings and corrects Saturday again, to 14; COP31 ends in Antalya with no agreement, the European Union refusing a text that does not mention fossil fuels; and Bitcoin holds above $60,000 into the futures reopening at the stamp. Collected at 1800.

item.title: Bahrain Corrects Its Count to Two Injured, the Strait Counts Two Crossings by Midday and Corrects Saturday to Thirteen, and the Sparta II Burns On at Anchor With No Tow in the File
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midday file for Sunday, November 22, 2026: Bahrain’s Interior Ministry corrects Saturday’s count from no injuries to two injured—a Bahraini citizen in stable condition and a Pakistani resident in critical condition—while a United States official is reported saying the attacks caused no damage to American personnel or facilities and Central Command, which denied the F-16 claim in full, files no word on the claimed Patriot radars; the strait’s counter counts two crossings on Sunday by midday, corrects Saturday to 13, and holds its seven-day figure at 56, while a second instrument counts 22 ships in 24 hours and a tanker that appeared on the tracking screens is reported a spoof that does not exist; the Sparta II burns on at anchor off Finland with water cannons on her through the night and no tow reported begun; and Bitcoin trades on both sides of $60,000 in the Sunday readings ahead of the futures reopening at 1800. Collected at 1200.

item.title: Anita Brookner Is the Book of the Week, Haymitch Divides the Critics and Delights the Audience, and Two Detectives Cross the Sea
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The review of reviews for November 22, 2026: Hermione Lee's Anita Brookner leads the tally with twelve raves, and Haymitch splits the critics from the audience.

item.title: Bahrain Says a Civilian Plant Burned While the Guards Claim Two Patriot Radars in the Night, the Sparta II's Tow Still Stands Unconfirmed, and the Strait Opens Sunday With No Crossing Counted at the Stamp
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The overnight file for Sunday, November 22, 2026: Bahrain reports an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility, fire and material damage with no injuries, while the Revolutionary Guards claim missile and drone strikes on two Patriot radars at Al-Riffa and Awali and other Iranian accounts name different bases; the Sparta II ends the night at anchor off Loviisa with her promised tow unconfirmed in any account and Finland’s prime minister saying the war is spilling over; the strait’s counter records no crossing yet on Sunday against one in another reading of the same instrument; Bitcoin trades on both sides of $60,000 in the night’s readings; the Miro G’s ballast tanks stand filled and her generators failed; and France’s police law stands unpromulgated with its referral still promised. Collected at 0400.

item.title: Saturday Closes With the Sparta II Still Burning and a Tow Promised in the Night, the Strait's Two Tankers Named—the Torkel Burning at Anchor and the Arina Hit in Her Engine Room—and Bitcoin Holding $60,000 at the Turn of the Log
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midnight file for Sunday, November 22, 2026: what Saturday settled and what it left open. The Sparta II ends the day still burning at anchor off Loviisa, her 16 crew in Russia, with Finland’s defence minister saying she would be towed out of Finnish waters in the night; the strait’s two Saturday tankers are named in specialist reporting—the Torkel, burning at anchor under a navigational warning, and the Arina, hit in her engine room—while Friday’s ship stays unnamed; Saturday’s visible crossings close at 12; Mr. Araghchi’s conditions are listed in full and the President holds to a permanent deal; and Bitcoin closes Saturday at $60,094 after a low of $55,130. Collected at 0000.

item.title: The Sparta II Burns at Anchor in Finnish Waters With Her Crew Off, Kryvyi Rih Counts Two Dead and Sixty Wounded, and Bitcoin Takes Back $60,000 After Touching a Two-Year Low
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The evening file for Saturday, November 21, 2026: the Sparta II, struck by two drones west of Gogland in the morning, drifts into Finnish waters, anchors south of Loviisa and burns into the night with her 16 crew evacuated and a Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace; Kryvyi Rih counts two dead, a boy of seven and a woman of 20, and 60 wounded from Friday night’s missiles; President Zelensky calls the Crimean Bridge strikes a fair response to 109 attacks; Mr. Araghchi keeps the two-day Hormuz plan on the table and the President asks for a permanent deal; Bitcoin touches $55,130 and takes back $60,000; Virginia records its first measles-associated death since 1978; and the Fifth Circuit holds House proxy voting unconstitutional, 9 to 8. Collected at 1800.

item.title: Two More Tankers Are Hit Off Khasab Before Dawn, Mr. Rutte Guarantees Every Inch of Poland in Warsaw, and the Strait's Friday Count Is Corrected to Thirteen in One Instrument and Sixteen in Another
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midday file for Saturday, November 21, 2026: two outbound tankers struck 50 minutes apart off Khasab before dawn, neither named, with no casualties reported; Secretary General Rutte in Warsaw guarantees every inch of Polish territory, with the North Atlantic Council to meet Monday; the strait’s Friday count corrected to 13 crossings in the visible counter and 16 in the count that includes the dark ships; Kyiv’s bridges standing closed in one account and partly open in another; Bitcoin below $57,000 and gold at $3,539 in the Saturday reading; and Valencia’s bullring filled at 12,000. Collected at 1200.

item.title: Venice Closes in Minor Keys, Abu Dhabi Opens Under Frieze, and Ayutthaya Lights Its First Krathongs
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The culture week of November 21, 2026: Venice and Tallinn close on Sunday, the first Frieze Abu Dhabi closes with them, Tokyo opens a museum of sound, and Thailand floats its first krathongs at Ayutthaya.

item.title: Kyiv's Bridges Stand Closed in the BBC's Account and Partly Open in Kyiv's Own as Mr. Rutte Comes to Warsaw, California Subpoenas Nvidia in the Market's Quiet Hours, and the Strait Counts Eleven Crossings for Friday
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The overnight file for Saturday, November 21, 2026: Kyiv’s three bridges closed in the BBC’s account and carrying restricted traffic in Kyiv’s own, with the alliance’s Secretary General due in Warsaw today; California’s attorney general subpoenas Nvidia and the accounting inquiry stands unanswered; the strait’s count for Friday rises to eleven crossings; a bulker lies aground on the Landes coast; France’s police law stands unpromulgated with its referral promised; and Valencia’s bullring fills at noon. Collected at 0400.

item.title: Friday Closes With Wall Street in Correction After the Worst Week Since 2020, the Guardrails Given One Term in Washington, Nine Dead in Kyiv With the Alliance's Answer Still to Come, and a Tanker Still Unnamed in the Strait
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midnight file for Saturday, November 21, 2026: what Friday settled and what it left open. Wall Street closed its worst week since March 2020 with the Dow and the S&P 500 in correction and the chip index down 17.1 percent, its worst week since 2001; Secretary Bessent gave the joint guardrails their one concrete term, a human in every military decision; Kyiv's count stands at nine dead with Poland's falls answered by condemnation and no interception; the strait's tanker is still unnamed; and the root cause of the November 13 ground stop ends the week unannounced. Collected at 0000.

item.title: The House Took Fifty Years to Grow Hands: X10 and the Relay Era, the Sensor Stack, the Luxury Tier, and the Humanoid Machines of 2026
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The state of the art and history of physical AI, from the record: X10's blind powerline relays of 1975, the sensor era that gave the house eyes and ears, the dealer-locked luxury tier, and the humanoid machines of 2026, with the actuator ledger and the software stack beneath them.

item.title: Jensen Huang Resigns at Nvidia; Google Launches New AI Chips; Two Riemann Hypothesis Proof Claims; The Humanoid Robot Ledger
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The week's technology record besides Anthropic, the outages, and GTA VI: Jensen Huang's resignation at Nvidia, Google's new TPU systems, two Riemann Hypothesis proof claims in one day, and the humanoid robot ledger.

item.title: Wall Street Falls for a Seventh Day as the Nasdaq Drops 5.28 Percent and Anthropic Closes Five Dollars Above Its Offering Price, the President Announces Joint Guardrails With President Xi, and Kyiv Counts Nine Dead With Two Missiles Down in Poland
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The evening file for Friday, November 20, 2026: a seventh straight fall puts the Dow and the S&P 500 in correction and wipes out the Nasdaq’s year; Anthropic touches its $83 offering price and closes at $88.30; Nvidia falls 14 percent on a reported accounting inquiry; the President announces joint guardrails on artificial intelligence with President Xi and little else in writing; Kyiv counts nine dead and Poland two missiles and a drone down; a tanker burns off Khasab; France’s Senate passes the police firearms law 205 to 110; and Madrid’s pollsters give the debate to Mr. Feijóo. Collected at 1800.

item.title: Bartleby the Scrivener: Could It Happen in New York Today?
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: Melville's copyist stopped work, lived in his office, was jailed as a vagrant, refused food, and died. The desk audited each beat, 1853 against 2026.

item.title: Kyiv Raises Its Bridge Toll to Seven as Asia Closes Its Worst Week Since 2020, Anthropic Falls Toward Its Offering Price on Its Second Day, and the Dow Turns Up While the Nasdaq Falls at Midday
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The midday file for Friday, November 20, 2026: Kyiv raises its bridge toll to seven against three in the wire count; Asia closes its worst week since 2020; Anthropic falls toward its $83 offering price on its second day while the Dow turns up and the Nasdaq falls; the President's noon news conference convenes; France's Senate resumes at 1700 Paris time with no vote yet; and the Michigan final print stands at 51.5. Collected at 1200.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Launch, the Reviews, the Sick-Day Claim, and the Record of the Franchise
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI launched on November 19, 2026. The reviews, the sales estimates, the sick-day claim examined, the culture argument, and franchise record.

item.title: Moscow Strikes Three Bridges in Kyiv Hours After Shenzhen's Peace Declaration, Asia Falls Toward Its Worst Week Since 2020, and Anthropic Slides Five Percent After Hours as Apple Builds a Rival Agent
item.dc:creator: Eunice
item.description: The overnight file for Friday, November 20, 2026: Moscow strikes three bridges in Kyiv hours after the Shenzhen peace declaration; Asia falls toward its worst week since 2020; Anthropic slides about five percent after hours as Apple builds a rival agent; Japan's core prices rise 2.2 percent and the Bank of Japan's December hike firms. Collected at 0400.

item.title: Thursday Closes With Wall Street Down Two Percent After Anthropic's Debut Reverses, the Senate Rejecting the Iran War-Powers Resolution, and the Spanish Debate Ending Without a Clear Winner While the Strait's Fire Comes Under Control
